why_wrong.o2: Sentence 2 is about fees; no period of time has been mentioned yet.
why_wrong.o4: "For this reason" in sentence 4 needs the hardship stated before it, so the new sentence must come before 4, not after.

"Among the oldest are words from Hokkien Chinese, brought by traders long before the Spanish arrived."

why_wrong.o3: After sentence 3 the paragraph has moved on to Spanish; going back to the oldest borrowings breaks the order.

A coastal cooperative in Sorsogon sold dried fish through three neighborhood stalls. Each stall recorded how much stock arrived, how much sold, and how much remained. One stall appeared to perform poorly because it had more unsold stock than the others. The manager initially proposed cutting its allocation. During a review, however, workers showed that the stall had received a much larger shipment on the final day of the reporting period. Those boxes had not yet been displayed for sale. Once the manager separated stock available for several days from stock delivered just before closing, the apparent gap narrowed. The cooperative decided to report sell-through rates using stock that had actually been offered to customers, while still keeping a separate record of all deliveries. The goal was not to make every stall appear successful, but to compare performance fairly. The cooperative asked each vendor to record when a shipment first reached the display shelf.

Why was the original comparison between stalls potentially misleading?

options.text: The stall's vendors had recorded their daily sales carelessly.
The other two stalls had hidden some unsold boxes from the manager.
One stall's late shipment had not yet been put out for sale.
The manager had already cut that stall's allocation before the review.

reveal.terms: Inference: a conclusion the passage supports without stating it word for word.
reveal.shortcut: Look for the sentence with "however": it names what the first comparison missed.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: "One stall's late shipment had not yet been put out for sale." The larger shipment arrived on the last day and was never displayed, so those leftovers had no fair chance to sell.

why_wrong.o1: The passage never questions the vendors' records; the problem was timing.
why_wrong.o2: Nothing suggests any stall hid stock.
why_wrong.o4: He only proposed the cut; the review came first and changed the plan.

The public hospital in Legazpi began asking patients whether they received their laboratory results within the promised time. A simple satisfaction survey first showed unusually high approval. A clerk later noticed that survey forms were offered only at the counter where completed results were collected. Patients still waiting for results rarely passed that counter, so their experiences were missing. The quality team moved the survey link to appointment slips and allowed patients to answer even when a result was delayed. It also added an option to say that the result had not yet arrived. After that change, the reported percentage of timely results fell, although the hospital's laboratory procedures had not changed during the same week. The director explained that a more complete sample can make performance look worse while producing a more accurate measure. She instructed staff to review the delays rather than blame patients for giving negative feedback.

What best explains the decrease in the reported on-time result rate?

options.text: The laboratory took longer to release results that same week.
Patients still waiting for results could now answer the survey.
Patients gave negative answers to protest the new appointment slips.
Fewer patients answered once the survey moved to appointment slips.

reveal.terms: Inference: explain a result using what the passage states.
reveal.shortcut: Ask who could answer before and after the change.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: "Patients still waiting for results could now answer the survey." Moving the survey to appointment slips let waiting patients answer, so the sample now included the delays the first survey missed.

why_wrong.o1: The passage says laboratory procedures had not changed that week.
why_wrong.o3: No protest is mentioned; the director told staff not to blame patients.
why_wrong.o4: The passage never says the number of answers fell.

A group of science teachers in Butuan asked students to measure how much rain fell in containers placed around the school. The students used identical containers, but one was placed below a roof edge that sometimes poured extra water into it. That container consistently recorded higher levels after a storm. Some students immediately concluded that the western side of the campus always received more rainfall. Their teacher pointed out the drainage channel above the container and asked whether the setup was measuring rainfall alone. The class moved the container to an open space and repeated the observation over several storms. The difference became smaller, although the students still found some variation between sites. In their report, the class separated what was measured directly from explanations that remained tentative. They described the placement problem as a source of bias rather than dismissing all their work. The class recorded the exact position of each container and kept photographs of the setup for future students.

Which factor most clearly undermined the original comparison?

options.text: The western side of the campus really does receive more rain.
The students read the containers at different times after each storm.
Water from the roof edge added to one container's rainfall.
One container was a different size from the others that were used.

reveal.terms: Inference: identify what weakened a comparison.
reveal.shortcut: The teacher's question (was it measuring rainfall alone?) points to the cause.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: "Water from the roof edge added to one container's rainfall." The container below the roof edge caught runoff as well as rain, so it measured more than the rainfall at that spot.

why_wrong.o1: The passage treats that conclusion as hasty; the gap shrank once the container was moved.
why_wrong.o2: Reading times are never mentioned.
why_wrong.o4: The students used identical containers.

The provincial archives in La Union invited residents to submit photographs of old streets. Many contributors remembered where a photo had been taken but not the exact year. Instead of assigning a date based solely on the age of the buildings, the archivist recorded approximate time ranges and explained the uncertainty. When two photographs appeared to show the same celebration, volunteers compared shop signs, clothing, and the newspaper visible in one frame. They discovered that the pictures had been taken at similar events several years apart. The archives kept both images but revised their captions. At a public presentation, the archivist explained that preserving local history requires a clear distinction between a remembered account, a supported estimate, and a verified date. She encouraged contributors to share additional evidence while emphasizing that corrections would be documented openly rather than made without a record. Original photographs were stored separately from edited presentation copies.

Why did the archivist use approximate date ranges on some captions?

options.text: The evidence could not support an exact year for some photos.
Contributors had asked that their photos carry no exact dates.
The age of the buildings already showed the precise year of each photo.
Ranges let the archives avoid having to revise any captions later.

reveal.terms: Inference: explain a choice from the facts the passage gives.
reveal.shortcut: Find what contributors could not remember, then why a range is used instead.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: "The evidence could not support an exact year for some photos." Contributors often remembered places but not years, so the archivist recorded ranges rather than claim a precision the evidence lacked.

why_wrong.o2: No contributor made such a request.
why_wrong.o3: The archivist declined to date photos from building age alone.
why_wrong.o4: The archives did revise captions, and corrections are documented openly.

A barangay in Iligan installed solar lights along a footpath used by students and vendors. The first inspection found that every lamp switched on at dusk. Two months later, residents reported that some sections were dark despite functioning bulbs. Workers discovered that newly grown branches were shading several panels during the day. The lights had too little stored energy to operate through the night. The maintenance plan was updated to include checks of sunlight exposure, battery condition, and the path itself. Residents were also given an easy way to report which lamp had failed and when. The chairperson said installation was only the beginning of public service. Equipment must continue working in changing conditions, and maintenance records are essential when deciding whether the design needs improvement or a repair is sufficient. The maintenance team asked residents to report the specific lamp location instead of simply saying that the path was dark.

What caused some lights to fail despite working bulbs?

Shaded panels could not store enough energy for the night.
Residents had switched off some lamps to save electricity.
The first inspection had missed lamps that never switched on.

A cooperative of rice growers in Isabela began publishing prices offered by several buyers. The bulletin helped farmers negotiate, but some complaints arose because one displayed price included transport to the mill while another assumed delivery by the farmer. The numbers appeared directly comparable even though the conditions differed. To fix this, the cooperative added columns for delivery location, required moisture level, payment date, and deductions. It also marked which prices were offers rather than completed sales. Members said that the more detailed bulletin was harder to scan quickly, so staff created a short summary with a link to the full conditions. The manager explained that a useful comparison must be both easy to read and fair. Leaving out an important condition can make a simple number more misleading than a longer explanation. The cooperative encouraged members to ask buyers clarifying questions before accepting offers. A farmer reading only the headline price could otherwise agree to transportation or moisture terms that reduced the final payment.

Which change most directly improved the fairness of the price comparison?

Showing only the highest offer from each buyer every week
Listing each offer's delivery, moisture, payment and deductions
Asking buyers to post one price that covers every delivery term

why_wrong.o2: The cooperative never limited the bulletin to top offers.

A volunteer suggested assigning every household the same priority to appear fair. The nurse explained that equal treatment does not always mean identical scheduling: some patients had only one day's supply left while others had enough for several weeks. The office began recording remaining medicine, accessibility of each route, and the date of the next expected delivery. Staff continued to explain how priorities were set and allowed households to report errors in their records. During an emergency, the nurse said, transparent criteria were important both for urgent care and public trust. The office still sought to serve all households, but the order of delivery reflected the severity of immediate need and the feasibility of safe transport. The nurse emphasized that a transparent priority rule should still allow correction when a record is outdated.

Why did the nurse reject identical delivery priority for all households?

options.text: Giving every household the same priority would make the records too long to keep.
Households differed in medicine left and in how safely they could be reached.
Remote households had asked to be served after the town center.
Treating everyone identically is unfair in every situation.

reveal.shortcut: The nurse's explanation follows the colon: supplies differed.

New systems are best tested during quiet hours to avoid disruption.
Clinics should cut down how often patients need to speak with reception.
A new service should work for all patients in everyday conditions.

items.stem: A report says errors fell after peer review, but it does not compare other offices. The safest inference is:

options.text: Peer review may have contributed to the decline
Peer review alone caused every improvement
Errors will never return
Other offices cannot use peer review

reveal.terms: The right answer is stated in the passage or follows directly from it, without adding claims the text does not make.
reveal.shortcut: Without a comparison group, a before-and-after change suggests a possible cause, not proof.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: "Peer review may have contributed to the decline". The before-and-after association supports a cautious possibility, not proof of sole causation.

why_wrong.o2: "Alone" and "every" claim proof the report does not give.
why_wrong.o3: Nothing supports a permanent prediction.
why_wrong.o4: Other offices were not studied, so nothing is said about them.

items.stem: If a memo says the pilot served 30 of 40 applicants, what fraction were served?

options.text: Three-fourths
One-fourth
Two-fifths
Four-thirds

reveal.terms: The right answer is stated in the passage or follows directly from it, without adding claims the text does not make.
reveal.shortcut: Served ÷ total, then simplify: 30/40 = 3/4.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: "Three-fourths". Thirty divided by forty simplifies to three-fourths.

why_wrong.o2: One-fourth (10 of 40) is the share NOT served.
why_wrong.o3: Two-fifths would be 16 of 40, which does not match 30 of 40.
why_wrong.o4: Four-thirds divides total by served (40/30), which is upside down.
